name: Íslandsbanki Reykjavik Marathon
typicalWeather: About 8–15 °C, usually with a sea breeze
summary: The Íslandsbanki Reykjavik Marathon is held in August, on the same day as Reykjavik Culture Night. It is a single loop that starts at the University of Iceland on Sæmundargata and finishes by the harbor on Geirsgata. The course passes the sea, the Seltjarnarnes peninsula and the Elliðaárdalur valley.
courseHighlights: Start at the University of Iceland on Sæmundargata
Ægisíða and Seltjarnarnes by the sea
City centre and Sæbraut along the shore
Elliðaárdalur valley with a small waterfall and salmon river
Finish on Geirsgata by the harbor

paceStrategy.summary: The route mixes flat and rolling sections. A listing says the organiser describes it as 60% flat and 40% rolling, with hills mostly after 15 km. Run the first part evenly and be ready for small rises later. Weather is usually mild with a sea breeze.

segments.terrain: Seaside and city streets west to Seltjarnarnes and the centre, mostly flat
segments.advice: Run at goal pace and use the easier section well.

segments.terrain: Sæbraut, Laugardalur and the inland sections, where hills mostly start
Elliðaárdalur and the return along Sæbraut to the harbor
segments.advice: Hold steady and push over the last 3 km.

fuelingNotes: The official page lists 10 aid stations about every 4–5 km, subject to change. Plan a gel between stations and take one before the hills after 15 km.
tips: The organisers do not recommend the race for inexperienced runners
The route is exposed to the sea breeze, so wear a cap or sunglasses on sunny days
A new route is being prepared, so check the official map for the current course
The marathon is on Culture Night, so the city centre is busy

faq.question: Is the Reykjavik Marathon flat?
faq.answer: It is a mix. One listing says about 60% flat and 40% rolling, with hills mostly after 15 km. Sources do not give a reliable climb figure.

faq.question: Where does the Reykjavik Marathon start and finish?
faq.answer: It starts on Sæmundargata by the University of Iceland and finishes on Geirsgata by the harbor.

faq.question: When is the Reykjavik Marathon held?
faq.answer: It is held in August, on the same day as Reykjavik Culture Night.
